A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Chain & Hash work. Their main text, algorithms, figures, and appendices support reliable matching and comparison. Localized reporting errors in v3 do not prevent assessment of the substantive changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original fingerprint-verification, benchmark-utility, fine-tuning, quantization, and hyperparameter experiments in Section V and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments and adds LoRA adapter evaluations and a direct comparison with Xu et al.'s black-box fingerprinting method in Sections 7.5 and 7.10.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, random and natural question generation, meta-prompt augmentation, Anchor Loss, random padding, and verification remain substantively unchanged. Section 7.5 applies the existing procedure to LoRA adapters without specifying a new fingerprinting component or algorithmic rule.

E1.justification: Both versions use MMLU, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, TruthfulQA, Alpaca, and ChatDoc/HealthCareMagic-100k. The LoRA experiments reuse ChatDoc and the existing fingerprint-verification and meta-prompt tasks. They change model parameterization and evaluation settings without introducing new represented data, domains, or input scenarios.

E2.justification: V3 Section 7.10 adds Xu et al.'s black-box Instructional Fingerprinting to a direct Llama-3-Instruct comparison under the shared meta-prompt evaluation. V1 discussed that method and probed its released model, but did not include this controlled competing-method comparison. This substantially strengthens comparator coverage.

E3.justification: V3 adds a protocol that trains ChatDoc LoRA adapters, fingerprints them, and assesses utility through evaluation-set loss rather than the four general benchmarks. It also constructs ten Xu-method fingerprints for the new comparison. Existing full-model protocols are largely retained. V3's conflicting 7B and 8B base-model labels do not reliably establish an actual model replacement.

E4.justification: V3 extends meta-prompt robustness and question-type analyses to LoRA adapters and tests Xu's method against adversarial meta-prompts. V1's brief case study reducing a released model's trigger to a few tokens is omitted. Existing fine-tuning, quantization, six-meta-prompt, and 100-question analyses remain; the collusion discussion is relocated rather than newly evaluated.

E5.justification: Both versions describe three independently fingerprinted instances and retain the same probability-based reporting practices. Neither adds seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The 99% verification-success target remains an evaluation criterion, not a newly introduced confidence interval.

E6.justification: V3 Figures 5 and 10 add LoRA verification results. Section 7.10 newly reports Xu-method strength below 0.04 for Courteous and below 10^-4 for the other challenging meta-prompts. Existing benchmark plots and all 48 fine-tuning trial values are retained. Section 7.5 also reports adapter utility results, but its Llama-3 exception ends at 'approximately 14' without a unit, preventing precise interpretation.

T1.justification: V1 Section VI.E's quantitative argument connecting roughly 41% per-question success in a ten-question chain to a 95% chance of two successful questions is omitted. The hash construction and joint-matching security argument remain substantively unchanged, and v3 adds no formal security proof.

C1.justification: V3's abstract and introduction add an explicit claim of applicability to LoRA adapters. Cryptographically linked fingerprints, black-box verification, adversarial meta-prompt robustness, and utility preservation were already central claims in v1. Their presentation as two main contributions largely reorganizes existing claims.

C2.justification: V3 attributes comparable LoRA fingerprinting performance across model sizes to similarly sized adapters, qualifying the retained full-model capacity interpretation. It omits v1's Phi-3-specific limitation concerning meta-prompt and non-fingerprinted-input requirements and the proposed hybrid-question direction. Core black-box, leakage, and gray-box-access qualifications remain.

D1.justification: V3 newly discloses a virtual machine with eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs. It removes v1's explicit dataset-size descriptions and explanation of using non-fingerprinted questions similar to fingerprint questions. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish corresponding changes to the retained experiments.

R1.justification: V3 removes four output-watermarking references and the 'Simple probes can catch sleeper agents' reference while retaining the principal fingerprinting literature. Section 2.2 adds a priority claim for comprehensive adversarial-evaluation guidelines, including meta-prompts and relevance to backdoors. Xu et al. is retained and newly evaluated, not newly cited.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, requirements, and much of the evaluation are extensively rewritten. Threat Model and Fingerprinting become separate main sections, instruction-tuned model evaluations are consolidated, collusion moves into Evaluation, and Discussion and Limitations is shortened. This is substantial restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The overview is redrawn with three illustrative questions instead of four. Existing experiment panels are merged and reordered, v1 Figure 9 becomes v3 Table 1 with unchanged values, and hyperparameter plots move from the appendix into the main text. New LoRA figures and extensive caption, typography, and layout changes further alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: The direct Xu-method comparison provides additional evidence for the central adversarial meta-prompt argument, while the LoRA experiments support broader applicability. Table 1 also makes the retained trial counts easier to compare than v1's heavily capped bar plots. These provide a limited net improvement, tempered by sparse LoRA implementation details, the incomplete utility result in Section 7.5, and removal of some useful technical and limitation discussion.
